PLINKO

Released: June 2026 | Edge: 1.00%

Provably Fair
Plinko

A ball drops from the top of a peg board, bounces left or right once per row, and lands in one of the buckets along the bottom. The bucket it lands in is your multiplier. That is the whole game, and everything you control sits in two settings: how many rows the ball falls through, from 8 to 16, and which risk level shapes the buckets. Plinko is one of the LIQD Originals, returns 99% on every board, and carries a fourth risk level, WTF, that no other Plinko has.

How To Play Plinko

You set rows and risk, enter a stake and press Bet. The ball starts above the centre peg and bounces once per row on its way down, so a 16-row board has 17 buckets at the bottom. The middle buckets are where most balls end up, because far more routes through the pegs lead there than to the edges. The edges are rare for the same reason, which is why they hold the big numbers.

Each drop settles the moment the ball lands. There is no round to finish and no waiting for the previous ball: you can have several in the air at once, each a separate bet. Changing rows or risk while balls are falling only affects the next drop.

Speed has three settings: Normal shows the full bounce, Quick shortens it, Turbo cuts it to the minimum. In any speed you can hold the space bar instead of clicking and the game streams balls for as long as you hold. On Turbo with space held the board turns into a continuous stream of comets, the fastest way through a session without touching the mouse.

WTF Mode

WTF is the fourth risk level and the reason people search for this Plinko. Select it and the row picker locks at 13, giving you a 14-bucket board where the ten middle buckets pay nothing and show a skull instead of a number. The two buckets next to the edges pay 235x, the two outermost pay 1,000x. Four paying buckets, ten that eat the stake.

The maths of a 13-row board is fixed, so the odds are exact. Each 1,000x bucket lands one drop in 8,192, so the pair comes up once every 4,096 drops. Each 235x bucket lands 13 drops in 8,192, so that pair hits once every 315 drops. Put together, a WTF drop pays something once every 293 drops and returns nothing the other 99.66% of the time. The board still holds 99% RTP: the rare hits are sized to pay back what the skulls take, which makes it the highest-variance Plinko configuration that exists.

Over 1,000 drops, the chance of landing at least one paying bucket is about 97%, and the chance of at least one 1,000x is about 22%. WTF is the Plinko equivalent of the maximum-volatility modes slot studios sell as god mode: long stretches of nothing, then a single ball that pays for all of them, or does not.

How The Boards Compare

Rows and risk set the shape of the payout strip. More rows means more buckets, rarer edges and higher edge multipliers; higher risk pulls value out of the middle and into those edges. The three standard levels follow the industry-standard Plinko tables at 99% RTP, and WTF is the LIQD board.

Every board returns the same 99%. What changes is how it arrives: Low at 8 rows pays small amounts on nearly every drop, High at 16 rows keeps the value in two buckets that hit once in 32,768, and WTF removes the small payouts entirely.

Play Plinko For Free

The demo on this page runs every board, including WTF, on the same 99% tables and the same provably fair engine as the real-money game. You play at a zero stake rather than with play money, so every demo drop still appears in your bet history and can be verified like any other. It is the quickest way to see what a WTF session looks like before you stake anything.

Verifying A Drop

Every drop comes from the same provably fair scheme that runs Mines and Blackjack: a server seed committed as a hash before you bet, a client seed you can set yourself, and a nonce that increments each drop. The game runs HMAC-SHA256 over those inputs and the result decides the bucket the ball lands in. The bucket is fixed before the ball appears. The animation only shows it getting there.

After you rotate your server seed, the previous seed is revealed and you can recheck any drop from its bet details: hash the revealed seed to confirm it matches the pre-drop commitment, then rerun the HMAC with your seed and nonce. The Verify tab takes rows and risk as inputs and highlights the bucket the ball landed in, so you can check a WTF skull as easily as a 1,000x.

Quick Answers

What is WTF mode in Plinko? A fourth risk level on LIQD Plinko, fixed at 13 rows, where the ten middle buckets pay zero and only the four outer buckets pay, at 235x and 1,000x. It holds 99% RTP and is the highest-variance Plinko board available.

Does the number of rows change the RTP? No. Every combination of rows and risk returns 99%. Rows change how many buckets there are and how far apart the small and large multipliers sit.

Is there a Plinko strategy? No. The bucket is fixed by the provably fair seed before the ball appears, so no drop timing, row switching or bet pattern changes where it lands. The only choice that matters is which board you play, and that changes how often you win, not how much you get back over time.

How do I know if a drop is fair? Every drop is derived from a server seed committed before you bet and a client seed you control, and any past drop can be recomputed from its bet details.

Before You Play

The 99% is the same on every board, so the only decision on this page is how you want that 1% to be taken from you: a sliver off most drops on Low, or everything off nearly every drop on WTF with the odd 1,000x to make it back. Bankroll for the board you pick. A WTF session that ends before drop 293 has, on average, not seen a paying bucket yet.

PROVABLY FAIR

You don’t have to trust us.

We lock in our half of the result before you bet.

VERIFY A ROUND
Three Ingredients
Server Seed

Hidden Until Revealed

A random secret we generate for you. While it’s in use you see only its hash. That hash is our up-front commitment.

Client Seed

Always Visible

Random by default, yours to change to anything. Your control over it is what stops a result being manipulated in advance.

Nonce

Automatic

A simple counter that ticks up with every bet, so the same pair of seeds never gives the same result twice.

Outcome
=
Server Seed
+
Client Seed
+
Nonce

Combined with HMAC-SHA256. One-way, deterministic, checkable by anyone.

Play, Reveal & Verify.

The whole system is one loop. Open the Provably Fair modal on any Originals game to run it.

Commit

Before you bet

You can see your client seed, the hash of our server seed, and how many bets you’ve made on the pair.

Play

Each bet takes a nonce

While a server seed is in play, we keep it hidden. If you could see it, you could see your next results too.

Reveal

When you rotate

We hand over the old server seed in full, and a new one (already hashed) takes its place. To see a seed, you retire it.

Verify

Anyone, any time

Take a revealed seed pair and a nonce and run them back through. Same inputs, same result, every time.

ONE RULE.

You Can’t Rotate And Reveal While A Game Round Is Still In Progress, Otherwise You Could Read The Outcome Before It’s Revealed. Finish The Round First.

We Commit First

The hash is published before your first bet and can’t be changed afterwards. When the seed is revealed on rotation, it hashes back to exactly the commitment you were shown.
